newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo Nobel seeking long-term investors.
newsitem.headline: Akzo Nobel seeking long-term investors.

text.p: Akzo Nobel said on Thursday it had agreed to waive a two-year standstill agreement on the sale of Securum AB's 10.2 percent Akzo shareholding in the interests of a controlled placement with long-term institutional shareholders.
"We are looking for shareholders who will stay with us for a long time," Akzo Nobel chairman Cornelis van Lede told a results news conference.
Under the agreement, Swedish state-owned holding Securum, which acquired Akzo shares as part of Akzo's takeover of Nobel in 1993, was not able to divest its stake until May 1998.

However, Akzo had agreed to unlock the standstill on condition that the price was right and that the 10.2 percent shareholding was placed in such a manner that the stock price continued to develop favourably, Van Lede said.
In May 1996 Securum sold a three percent stake in Akzo, after a previous lock-up period of two years expired.
"What we saw then prior to the sell-off is that market expectations of a sale pushed down Akzo's share price," he said.
By agreeing to an early sale this time around this could be avoided, he said, adding that current market conditions were favourable.
The share placement will target long-term institutional investors and NV Arnhemsche Maatschappij, an Amsterdam-listed tax-friendly investment vehicle which currently holds an 8.6 percent Akzo stake.
The shares will not be offered for sale in America for technical reasons, Van Lede said.
Akzo said earlier Securum planned to sell its remaining Akzo shares through a bookbuilding procedure, expected to start after today's Amsterdam stock exchange close.
-- Lien van der Leij Amsterdam newsroom, +31 20 504 5000.
